answer: An agent registry mitigates Sybil attacks by tying identities to localized geochemical attestation. Probes validate presence by measuring carotenoid decay in dried saffron, dielectric permittivity in cured timber, and water salinity in an adjacent lagoon. Attackers face heavy capital expenditures deploying physical sensor nodes rather than duplicating software threads. However, localized weather anomalies can skew measurement baselines, causing false rejections of honest participants.
